name: Walt's Worm
imitates: A cranefly larva, grub or cased caddis; a plain dubbed-body fly that keeps catching trout in Pennsylvania and New York streams. This is the tyer's wire-weighted variant that blends Walt Young's method with Sawyer's Killer Bug materials.
recipe: Wool yarn made into dubbing (Patons Classic Wool), or Hare's Ear Plus

steps.text: Start the thread behind the eye and wrap touching turns back to the bend.
Put a drop of super glue on the thread wraps so the wire will not slip.
Start copper wire at the bend and wind it forward in touching turns.
Stop the wire about one eye length behind the eye and break off the leftover ends.
Dub the thread with the wool dubbing.
Wind the dubbing forward, forming a slight carrot shape.
Whip finish twice and cut the thread.
